chunks: Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Saeed ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a free woman who is under the ownership of a slave (as his wife), so she buys him. Would his marriage be invalidated? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because he is an owned slave who is not able to possess anything.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a marriage if a free woman buys her slave husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that the marriage between a free woman and her slave is dissolved upon her purchasing him, as the husband transitions into her slave and loses the independent legal capacity required to maintain the marital bond. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the husband's status as a distinct legal entity; once he becomes her property, the hierarchical distinction necessary for the marriage contract is nullified. The narration underscores the practical implications of manumission on family law, ensuring that the marital tie does not persist when the structural conditions of 'free man to free woman' are altered.

en.hubeali: Abu Al Abbas Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, from Safwan, from Saeed Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a free woman who happened to be under the owned slave (as a wife), so she bought him. Would his marriage be invalidated?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, because he is an owned slave, not be able upon anything’.
